correctness.rationale: The graph Čech definition at odd scale three is instantiated exactly as the published generator formula requires: one generating simplex N_1[v] union N_1[w] for each hypercube edge. The verifier exhaustively constructs 3,944 nonempty faces and 18,800 Hasse covers, verifies an acyclic matching with critical counts one in dimension 0, one in dimension 3, and 24 in dimension 4, and computes every signed Morse boundary coefficient from dimension 4 to the unique dimension-3 cell as zero. Therefore the Morse 3-skeleton is a 3-sphere and each 4-cell attaching map has degree zero. Since homotopy classes of maps from a 3-sphere to a 3-sphere are classified by degree, all 24 attachments are null-homotopic. Modular homology over three primes independently gives Betti vector (1,0,0,1,24,0,0,0), agreeing with the published integral ranks. The proof is finite and exhaustive only for the stated 16-vertex complex.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source reports only the integral homology of the exact complex and explicitly says the remaining table entries, including this case, are not known there up to homotopy type. A later dissertation treats related Hamming-layer Čech complexes and poses wedge-of-3-spheres-and-4-spheres behavior as future work rather than proving this exact hypercube case. Targeted searches for the exact complex, aliases, sphere multiplicities, and equivalent hypercube notation found no stronger published or indexed statement.
residual_risks: An obscure or unindexed duplicate computation could exist outside the searched literature. This risk is reduced by the exact-notation searches and by the primary source's explicit statement that this table entry was not known there up to homotopy type.
The 2024 dissertation contains related conjectural structure, so future or unpublished follow-up work may independently reach the same special case; no such published coverage was located.

value.rationale: This is the smallest hypercube scale-three Čech case for which the cited primary paper records mixed degree-3/degree-4 homology but not the homotopy type. Determining it exactly resolves a natural named table entry, upgrades known Betti data to an attaching-map-level statement, and supplies a concrete base case for later conjectural wedge-of-3-spheres-and-4-spheres behavior. The result is not a routine recomputation: the substantive content is the exhaustive acyclic Morse reduction and the vanishing of all 24 attaching degrees.
